sourcesRead.title: MAUVE: Measuring the Gap Between Neural Text and Human Text using Divergence Frontiers (Pillutla, Swayamdipta, Zellers, Thickstun, Welleck, Choi, Harchaoui; NeurIPS 2021)
Trading Off Diversity and Quality in Natural Language Generation (Zhang, Duckworth, Ippolito, Neelakantan)
A Systematic Characterization of Sampling Algorithms for Open-ended Language Generation (Nadeem, He, Cho, Glass; AACL-IJCNLP 2020)
Automatic Detection of Generated Text is Easiest when Humans are Fooled (Ippolito, Duckworth, Callison-Burch, Eck; ACL 2020)
Is Temperature the Creativity Parameter of Large Language Models? (Peeperkorn, Kouwenhoven, Brown, Jordanous; ICCC 2024)

claims.claim: Pillutla and colleagues report that MAUVE scores greedy decoding at .016 on web text from GPT-2 XL, the lowest of the three decoding algorithms they compare.
claims.source: Pillutla, Swayamdipta, Zellers, Thickstun, Welleck, Choi, Harchaoui, 'MAUVE', arXiv:2102.01454v3 (2021); NeurIPS 2021
claims.quote: the lowest quality to greedy decoding (.016)
claims.page: Section 4.1, 'MAUVE identifies quality differences between decoding algorithms'; Table 3
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 XL and Grover, observation 2021; register measured: web text, news and story continuations

claims.claim: Pillutla and colleagues report that nucleus sampling has a lower Type I error than ancestral sampling but a higher Type II error, meaning it fails to cover the spread of human text.
claims.source: Pillutla, Swayamdipta, Zellers, Thickstun, Welleck, Choi, Harchaoui, arXiv:2102.01454v3 (2021); NeurIPS 2021
claims.quote: nucleus sampling does not effectively cover the human text distribution
claims.modelEra: Grover and GPT-2, 2021; register measured: web text and news

claims.claim: Pillutla and colleagues state that some plausible human text simply cannot be produced by a truncation-based decoder such as nucleus sampling, which is the Type II error their measure is built to catch.
claims.source: Pillutla, Swayamdipta, Zellers, Thickstun, Welleck, Choi, Harchaoui, arXiv:2102.01454v3 (2021); NeurIPS 2021
claims.quote: cannot be generated by truncation-based decoding algorithms such as nucleus sampling
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 era, 2021; register: web text

claims.claim: Pillutla and colleagues report a Spearman rank correlation of 0.952 between MAUVE and human human-likeness judgments on web text, against 0.810 for generation perplexity and minus 0.167 for the repetition metric.
claims.source: Pillutla, Swayamdipta, Zellers, Thickstun, Welleck, Choi, Harchaoui, arXiv:2102.01454v3 (2021); NeurIPS 2021
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 sizes with ancestral and nucleus sampling, 214 Mechanical Turk workers, 2021; register measured: web text

claims.claim: Zhang, Duckworth, Ippolito and Neelakantan report a likelihood trap: past an inflection point the sentences a model rates as most likely are rated by human crowdworkers as lower in quality.
claims.source: Zhang, Duckworth, Ippolito, Neelakantan, 'Trading Off Diversity and Quality in Natural Language Generation', arXiv:2004.10450v1 (2020)
claims.quote: the highest likelihood sentences are of surprisingly low
claims.modelEra: dialogue and open-ended generation models, 2020; register measured: conversational responses rated by crowdworkers

claims.claim: Zhang and colleagues based the likelihood trap finding on 146 crowdworkers rating 100 sentences drawn across a range of model likelihoods.
claims.source: Zhang, Duckworth, Ippolito, Neelakantan, arXiv:2004.10450v1 (2020)
claims.modelEra: 2020; register measured: dialogue responses

claims.claim: Zhang and colleagues report that once decoding algorithms are compared at equal entropy, the quality of their samples is comparable over a wide range, and they diverge only in the low-entropy regime.
claims.source: Zhang, Duckworth, Ippolito, Neelakantan, arXiv:2004.10450v1 (2020)
claims.quote: when aligned on entropy, sample quality between all
claims.modelEra: 2020, twenty decoder-hyperparameter configurations; register measured: dialogue responses rated by crowdworkers

claims.claim: Zhang and colleagues report that in the low-entropy regime nucleus sampling beat top-k, which beat temperature sampling, on human quality ratings.
claims.source: Zhang, Duckworth, Ippolito, Neelakantan, arXiv:2004.10450v1 (2020)
claims.modelEra: 2020; register measured: dialogue responses

claims.claim: Zhang and colleagues' decoder comparison rests on over 38,000 paired ratings of almost 10,000 samples.
claims.source: Zhang, Duckworth, Ippolito, Neelakantan, arXiv:2004.10450v1 (2020)
claims.modelEra: 2020; register measured: dialogue responses

claims.claim: Nadeem, He, Cho and Glass report that top-k, nucleus and tempered sampling perform on a par with one another in their human quality-diversity evaluation.
claims.source: Nadeem, He, Cho, Glass, 'A Systematic Characterization of Sampling Algorithms for Open-ended Language Generation', arXiv:2009.07243v1 (2020); AACL-IJCNLP 2020
claims.quote: are on par with each other
claims.modelEra: GPT2-small 110M fine-tuned on Gigaword and Wikitext-103, 602 Mechanical Turk crowdworkers, 2020; register measured: news sentences and Wikipedia prose

claims.claim: Nadeem and colleagues identify entropy reduction, order preservation and slope preservation as the three properties shared by top-k, nucleus and tempered sampling.
claims.source: Nadeem, He, Cho, Glass, arXiv:2009.07243v1 (2020); AACL-IJCNLP 2020
claims.quote: are shared among them: entropy reduction
claims.modelEra: GPT2-small fine-tuned on Gigaword and Wikitext-103, 2020; register: news and Wikipedia prose

claims.claim: Nadeem and colleagues report that sampling algorithms violating one of their three identified properties suffered a large drop on the quality-diversity trade-off, while new algorithms satisfying all three matched the existing ones.
claims.source: Nadeem, He, Cho, Glass, arXiv:2009.07243v1 (2020); AACL-IJCNLP 2020
claims.modelEra: GPT2-small fine-tuned on Gigaword and Wikitext-103, 2020; register measured: news sentences and Wikipedia prose

claims.claim: Ippolito, Duckworth, Callison-Burch and Eck argue that the improvement in decoding methods has chiefly been an improvement at fooling human readers, bought by introducing statistical abnormalities a machine detector can find.
claims.source: Ippolito, Duckworth, Callison-Burch, Eck, 'Automatic Detection of Generated Text is Easiest when Humans are Fooled', arXiv:1911.00650v2 (2020); ACL 2020
claims.quote: fooling humans. This comes at the expense of
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 large, observation 2019-2020; register measured: web text excerpts

claims.claim: Ippolito and colleagues measure that top-k sampling puts as much as 80 per cent of its probability mass in the 500 most common token types, where nucleus sampling, untruncated sampling and human text need at least 1,100 token types to reach the same share.
claims.source: Ippolito, Duckworth, Callison-Burch, Eck, arXiv:1911.00650v2 (2020); ACL 2020
claims.quote: up to 80% of its mass in the first 500 most
claims.page: Section 4, 'Why are top-k's samples so easy to detect?'; Figure 2b
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 large with k=40, observation 2019-2020; register measured: web text excerpts

claims.claim: Ippolito and colleagues report that even on 192-token multi-paragraph excerpts their human raters reached only 71.4 per cent accuracy at telling generated from human text.
claims.source: Ippolito, Duckworth, Callison-Burch, Eck, arXiv:1911.00650v2 (2020); ACL 2020
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 large, human raters 2019-2020; register measured: web text excerpts

claims.claim: Ippolito and colleagues state in their abstract that multi-sentence excerpts still fooled expert human raters more than thirty per cent of the time.
claims.source: Ippolito, Duckworth, Callison-Burch, Eck, arXiv:1911.00650v2 (2020); ACL 2020
claims.quote: fool expert human raters over 30% of the time.
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 large, 2019-2020; register measured: web text excerpts

claims.claim: Peeperkorn, Kouwenhoven, Brown and Jordanous find only a weak positive correlation between temperature and the novelty of generated stories.
claims.source: Peeperkorn, Kouwenhoven, Brown, Jordanous, 'Is Temperature the Creativity Parameter of Large Language Models?', arXiv:2405.00492v1 (2024); ICCC 2024
claims.quote: temperature is weakly correlated with novelty
claims.modelEra: Llama 2-Chat 70B quantised Q6_K, temperatures .001 to 2.0, 36 human participants, observation May 2024; register measured: short generated narratives

claims.claim: Peeperkorn and colleagues conclude that temperature's influence on creativity is far weaker and more nuanced than the label creativity parameter implies.
claims.source: Peeperkorn, Kouwenhoven, Brown, Jordanous, arXiv:2405.00492v1 (2024); ICCC 2024
claims.quote: far more nuanced and weak than suggested by
claims.modelEra: Llama 2-Chat 70B, May 2024; register measured: short generated narratives

claims.claim: Peeperkorn and colleagues report that for their fixed prompt and model the outputs at higher temperature did not sit semantically further from the greedy exemplar story than the outputs at lower temperature.
claims.source: Peeperkorn, Kouwenhoven, Brown, Jordanous, arXiv:2405.00492v1 (2024); ICCC 2024
claims.quote: for this specific prompt and model, is unable
claims.modelEra: Llama 2-Chat 70B, temperatures .001-2.0, May 2024; register measured: short generated narratives

claims.claim: Peeperkorn and colleagues report that raising temperature above 1.0 did not necessarily produce more diversity in their generated stories, as measured by normalised edit distance from the exemplar.
claims.source: Peeperkorn, Kouwenhoven, Brown, Jordanous, arXiv:2405.00492v1 (2024); ICCC 2024
claims.quote: higher temperatures (t > 1.0) do not necessarily lead
claims.modelEra: Llama 2-Chat 70B with plain temperature sampling, seven values from .001 to 2.0, May 2024; register measured: short generated narratives
